claims.finding: Second-quarter revenue was already released on 2026-07-23 (a 6-K, recorded in the corpus as a 'Q2 26 Earnings Results & Recap' with a -0.5% reaction), so the 2026-09-03 release - two 6-Ks the same morning - carries the half-year profit-and-loss, margins and any outlook rather than the top line; the revenue surprise, which is what usually moves a luxury name, is already in the price.
claims.corpus_ref: filings.json 6-K entries dated 2026-07-23 and two dated 2026-09-03; docs/43f565083d963dd453a2e5a3a2e636882ad642e2.txt entry dated 2026-07-23T11:59:21Z
claims.why_not_priced: The split-release structure (revenue in July, full accounts in September) is standard for European issuers and is exactly why the baseline's small median reactions look the way they do - but it is also why the run-in matters more than the print. The unpriced element is the composition: with revenue known, the entire surprise sits in gross margin and operating leverage at a wholesale-exposed luxury group, and there is no news search for this ticker (n_queries=0 in every admissible sweep) and no consensus anywhere in the capture to anchor a margin expectation.
claims.independence: none - this rests on the filing cadence and one Stocktwits line from the same document.

claims.finding: The stock fell 17.4% over twenty sessions and 8.5% over the last five into the print, on 848,200 shares a day, with no filing after a 6-K on 2026-08-24 and a passive 13G/A on 2026-08-12, no insider activity since 2026-05-11, and an admissible social stream containing exactly one message in the six weeks before the event.
claims.corpus_ref: baseline tape (run_up_5d -8.52%, run_up_20d -17.42%); filings.json shows nothing between 2026-08-24 and the print
claims.why_not_priced: A 17% de-rating with no company disclosure, no insider action and effectively zero observed commentary is an unexplained move, and unexplained moves into a print are more often information than noise. The honest alternative is that it is a sector de-rating - the same run also shows lululemon falling and a broader consumer-discretionary drawdown - in which case it carries no company-specific content, and that is why I keep this small.
claims.independence: The LULU capture in this same run records a coincident luxury and premium-apparel de-rating from a different set of sources, which supports the sector rather than the company reading - see the LULU hunt file's 'Lululemon cuts 2026 forecast as sales slump across Americas' item.
